## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Sorting
//
// The ordering vocabulary: a stable sorted-permutation function and the sorted
// array it induces. `SortedIndices` is the primary form — construction passes
// (convex hulls, median-split trees) need to map sorted positions back to
// source indices, which a sorted copy loses.
//
// These are reference bodies, not intrinsics: they are expressible from the
// existing kernel (plato-378 admission rule), so backends recover native speed
// through the override table (plato-368), not by growing the intrinsic list.
// See tracker/decisions/2026-08-04-spatial-structure-construction-in-plato.md.
//
// The algorithm is bottom-up merge sort over an index buffer: O(n log n),
// stable (ties keep source order because the left run wins them), and free of
// recursion, which the body contract requires (GLSL forbids recursion).
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merge_sort#Bottom-up_implementation

library Sorting
{
    // The permutation that sorts `xs`: element k of the result is the index of
    // the k-th smallest element of `xs` under `lessOrEqual`. Stable: equal
    // elements keep their source order. `lessOrEqual` must be a total order's
    // comparison (transitive, total); a partial or inconsistent comparer
    // yields an arbitrary permutation, never an out-of-range index.
    SortedIndices(xs: Array<$T>, lessOrEqual: Function2<$T, $T, Boolean>): Array<Integer>
    {
        var n = xs.Count;
        var src = new Buffer<Integer>(n);
        var i = 0;
        while (i < n)
        {
            src = src.Set(i, i);
            i = i + 1;
        }
        var dst = new Buffer<Integer>(n);
        var width = 1;
        while (width < n)
        {
            var lo = 0;
            while (lo < n)
            {
                var mid = (lo + width).Min(n);
                var hi = (lo + width + width).Min(n);
                var a = lo;
                var b = mid;
                var k = lo;
                // The nesting is load-bearing: `&&` is `And`, an ordinary
                // function of two evaluated arguments, so it does NOT
                // short-circuit — a combined condition would read past the
                // exhausted run.
                while (k < hi)
                {
                    if (a >= mid)
                    {
                        dst = dst.Set(k, src.At(b));
                        b = b + 1;
                    }
                    else if (b >= hi)
                    {
                        dst = dst.Set(k, src.At(a));
                        a = a + 1;
                    }
                    else if (lessOrEqual(xs[src.At(a)], xs[src.At(b)]))
                    {
                        dst = dst.Set(k, src.At(a));
                        a = a + 1;
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        dst = dst.Set(k, src.At(b));
                        b = b + 1;
                    }
                    k = k + 1;
                }
                lo = lo + width + width;
            }
            var merged = dst;
            dst = src;
            src = merged;
            width = width + width;
        }
        return src.Freeze();
    }

    // A new array holding the elements of `xs` in ascending `lessOrEqual`
    // order. Stable, as SortedIndices is. When positions matter — attributes
    // to carry along, source indices to report — use SortedIndices instead.
    Sort(xs: Array<$T>, lessOrEqual: Function2<$T, $T, Boolean>): Array<$T>
        => xs.SortedIndices(lessOrEqual).Map(i => xs[i]);
}
```
